_comment: Tier-2 for the SPARTA surface dependency chain, three claims in one deck. Nine wrong orderings are fed to the installed binary and each one aborts NON-ZERO with the message the knowledge quotes, verbatim including the (file:line) suffix: read_surf.cpp:73, surf.cpp:227, surf.cpp:230, surf.cpp:260, surf.cpp:343 twice, domain.cpp:100 and domain.cpp:253 twice. The partial-binding case is the load-bearing one — binding only 'group left surf id <= 25' of a 50-element data.circle reports 'ERROR: 25 surface elements not assigned to a collision model', so N is the count STILL UNBOUND, exactly as claimed, not the total. Four forms the entries call correct all run: correct_order, surf_collide declared before read_surf, both groups bound, and an 's' face bound with bound_modify. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 with SPARTA (24 Sep 2025). Skips when no binary is present, and the skip prints no expected key, so the runner records a failure rather than a pass. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 completes the partial surface binding -- the second group is bound to the collision model too -- so the deck is legal and cannot abort. That run goes from rc!=0 with "ERROR: 25 surface elements not assigned to a collision model (../surf.cpp:343)" to rc=0 with no message. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES (rc=0); with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS (rc=1) and these expect_in_output strings go False and disappear: every_wrong_ordering_aborts_nonzero=True, every_quoted_message_is_verbatim=True, partial_binding_reports_the_unbound_count_not_the_total=True. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/sparta/surface_command_dependency_chain && python source.py (passes, rc=0), then T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py (fails, rc=1). Needs a SPARTA binary: the fixtures find spa_serial/spa_mpi on PATH or at ~/Schreibtisch/sparta/src/spa_serial, else set SPARTA_BINARY; with none present they exit 0 on a SKIP: line.
